sentences.text: The Cordilleran ice sheet was a major ice sheet that periodically covered large parts of North America during glacial periods over the last ~ 2.6 million years .	ice sheet	ice sheet	North America	North America
Western Montana	Western Montana	Western Montana

The southwestern third or so of Yukon Territory	Yukon Territory	Yukon

The Alaska Peninsula	Alaska Peninsula	Alaska Peninsula
Almost all of the continental shelf north of the Strait of Juan de Fuca	continental shelf	continental shelf	Strait of Juan de Fuca	Strait of Juan de Fuca

The ice sheet covered up to 2.5 million square kilometres at the Last Glacial Maximum and probably more than that in some previous periods , when it may have extended into the northeast extremity of Oregon and the Salmon River Mountains in Idaho .	ice sheet	ice sheet	Last Glacial Maximum	Last Glacial Maximum	Oregon	Oregon
It is probable , though , that its northern margin also migrated south due to the influence of starvation caused by very low levels of precipitation .	starvation	starvation (glaciology)

At its eastern end the Cordilleran ice sheet merged with the Laurentide ice sheet at the Continental Divide , forming an area of ice that contained one and a half times as much water as the Antarctic ice sheet does today .	ice sheet	ice sheet	Laurentide ice sheet	Laurentide ice sheet	Continental Divide	Continental Divide of the Americas	Antarctic ice sheet	Antarctic ice sheet

At its western end it is believed nowadays that several small glacial refugia existed during the last glacial maximum below present sea level in the now-submerged Hecate Strait and on the Brooks Peninsula in northern Vancouver Island .	refugia	Last Glacial Maximum refugia	sea level	sea level	Hecate Strait	Hecate Strait	Brooks Peninsula	Brooks Peninsula	Vancouver Island	Vancouver Island

However , evidence of ice-free refugia above present sea level north of the Olympic Peninsula has been refuted by genetic and geological studies since the middle 1990s .	refugia	Last Glacial Maximum refugia	sea level	sea level	Olympic Peninsula	Olympic Peninsula
The ice sheet faded north of the Alaska Range because the climate was too dry to form glaciers .	ice sheet	ice sheet	Alaska Range	Alaska Range	glaciers	glaciers

Unlike the Laurentide ice sheet , which is believed to have taken as much as eleven thousand years to fully melt , it is believed the Cordilleran ice sheet , except for areas that remain glaciated today , melted very quickly , probably in four thousand years or less .	ice sheet	ice sheet	Laurentide ice sheet	Laurentide ice sheet

This rapid melting caused such floods as the overflow of Lake Missoula and shaped the topography of the extremely fertile Inland Empire of Eastern Washington .	floods	floods	Lake Missoula	Lake Missoula	Inland Empire	Inland Empire (Pacific Northwest)	Eastern Washington	Eastern Washington
